The spring salamander (Gyrinophilus porphyriticus) and the green salamander (Aneides aeneus) could also be adversely affected by the proposed impoundment and construction -- particularly the latter species, some of whose southernmost populations could be destroyed by the proposed Bad Creek impoundment (Applicant's Exhibit W). The longtailed salamander (Eurycea longicauda) and the coal skink (Eumeces authracinus) are listed as rare in Dr. Ingram's survey of herptiles of the Bad Creek area, and these species are classed as rare and peripheral in their North Carolina distribution (North Carolina Department of Natural and Economic Resources, 1973).
2.3 SOCIO-ECONOMIC CONSIDERATIONS
The four counties surrounding the proposed Bad Creek Project site are Oconee and Pickens Counties, South Carolina, and Jackson and Transylvania counties in North Carolina. The 1970 population for this 4-county area was 140,990, of which 99,684 were located in Oconee and Pickens Counties.
The town nearest the project site is Salem, South Carolina (1970 population 300) approximately 8 miles due south. Pickens, South Carolina (1970 population 2,954) is 17 miles southeast and Walhalla, South Carolina (1970 population 3,663) is about 18 miles southwest. Within a 50 mile radius of the project, two cities have populations greater than 50,000: Asheville, North Carolina (72,451), 42 miles northeast, and Greenville, South Carolina (157,073), 31 miles southeast. The area immediately surrounding the project is mountainous, rugged terrain with no resident population.
Despite the proximity of the project to North Carolina, the majority of its socio-economic impacts would most likely be felt in the South Carolina counties of Oconee and Pickens because of their dominance in terms of population and economic activity for the area surrounding the project. Thus, the socio-economic description and analysis that follows will concentrate on these two counties. The project itself would be located in Oconee County with the nearest population centers in Oconee and Pickens Counties. In addition, the Greenville-Spartanburg, South Carolina metropolitan area, which includes Pickens County, is the principal business and trading center for this region.
